Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.
Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.
Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.
Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.
"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said former Liverpool boss Klopp.
"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that."
Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job."
French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo has been named as Uefa's candidate to challenge Infantino.
Diallo received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee and formal ratification from the FFF is expected on Tuesday.
Uefa, which is European football's governing body, said it has "full confidence" Diallo would "uphold the highest standards of governance" amid its calls for "renewed unity and trust within the global football community".
Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead
Uefa has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.
It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.
The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.
Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.
"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," said Klopp.
"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.
"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it."

Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League game with Kosovo
T he Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up.
For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner.
This late lapse neatly captures the contradiction bedevilling this Ireland team under Hallgrímsson. Over the past 12 months, Ireland have been unmistakably better than they were during the dark days of the post-pandemic slump under Stephen Kenny. They have established a clear identity and pulled off a couple of phenomenal wins with a spine of players performing at an elite level, supplemented by emerging talent from the leagues below and beyond. Yet for all that, an acceptable level of success remains elusive for a team who have not managed to shake a maddening habit of self-sabotage.
They have a high ceiling, as they demonstrated a year ago. Last November they dismantled Portugal at the Aviva Stadium in a World Cup qualifier before booking their place in the playoffs with an unforgettable come-from-behind win against Hungary at the Puskas Arena.
In Budapest, the celebrations of a dramatic Troy Parrott hat-trick completed in the sixth minute of added time went viral and elevated the then AZ striker from being surplus to the requirements of a dreadful Tottenham to sought-after European household name. For the first time in almost a decade, Ireland were playing with something resembling swagger, spearheaded by a poster-boy striker apparently entering his prime.
Riding that wave, Ireland travelled to Prague last March for the playoff semi-final against Czechia, with Parrott striking again, from the penalty spot, as they set about taking an early 2-0 lead. What followed would become the lowest point of Hallgrímsson’s reign as Ireland sat back and invited pressure before conceding a needless penalty and subsequent late equaliser that preceded a crushing shootout defeat . Despite last summer’s expanded 48-team format in North America, poor game management had stymied Ireland’s chances of making the cut.
An uninspiring, but unbeaten, summer friendly window featured fairly routine low-profile wins over Grenada and Qatar and a 1-1 draw against the World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal. Having steadied the ship before this Nations League campaign, Ireland produced a performance in their opener against Kosovo little short of diabolical and went down to another late goal.
In the subsequent four fixtures, two overshadowed by loud protests over Ireland’s decision to honour matches against Israel , that same cycle of promise and frustration has played out on a loop.
The disappointment of defeat in Pristina was immediately cancelled out by a clinical dispatch of Israel in Debrecen. In Dublin, against Austria , Parrott struck twice to give Ireland a commanding first-half lead, but in a collapse that rather mirrored their nightmarish Prague experience, Ireland went on to relinquish control and were forced to settle for a disappointing draw.
Three days later they coughed up another lead in a bad-tempered 1-1 draw with Israel, their compulsion for throwing away cheap points from winning positions coming back to bite them. Although they never led against Austria on Saturday, when Caoimhín Kelleher made a series of excellent saves, the winner they conceded was ridiculously soft.
Hallgrímsson’s appointment in July 2024 after a drawn-out process lasting eight months came as a surprise. He has built a side with a strong, if occasionally gaffe-prone, backbone including Kelleher, the goalkeeper’s Brentford teammate Nathan Collins and the Ipswich defender Dara O’Shea. Jack Moylan, having the season of his life at Cardiff, has impressed in midfield, and Southampton’s Finn Azaz is an occasional, but unreliable, source of creative guile. Parrott, enjoying life in La Liga with Real Betis, has evolved from promising talent to undisputed focal point of the attack.
To his credit, Hallgrímsson has forged a clear, pragmatic identity that maximises his team’s strengths without any delusions of fancy-dan footballing grandeur against elite opposition. Under his watch, Ireland are rarely outclassed and carry a cutting edge sorely absent in the dying days of his predecessor’s tenure.
Unfortunately, an inability to concentrate for 90 minutes continues to be their undoing and the must-win Nations League group finale at the Aviva Stadium will provide the ultimate judgment on the past 12 months. With Austria guaranteed promotion to League A, Ireland still have second place and its promotion playoff spot within reach.
Victory over Kosovo would also secure a place in pot two for next month’s Euro qualifying draw in Belfast, whereas defeat could leave them flirting with a relegation playoff to the tournament’s third tier. As the only ever-present residents of the Nations League’s second tier, now may be the time for something finally to give.

Collins picked up a knee injury in the closing stages against Austria on Saturday
Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.
Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.
Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.
Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.
"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.
"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."
The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.
Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.
"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.
"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.
"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."
The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.
While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.
"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.
"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.
"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career
Andy Robertson will become Scotland's most capped men's international after being named in the starting XI for Monday's Nations League game in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country.
Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he will surpass his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years.
After moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.
But, in St Gallen, the spotlight will shine on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he moves solo at the summit.
Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King
For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.
'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1986 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.
Few since have even come close to toppling him - and Robertson is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.
"He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.
"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.
"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."
Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.
But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday took him to within six of the legendary duo.
The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.
Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 33 times more than any other player.
At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.
Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.
Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.
"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."
One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.
Perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.
Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.
"I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.
'I had him in my Fifa team!' - Findlay Curtis on going from fan to team-mate of Robertson
Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.
It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.
McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.
He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.
However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.
Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.
"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.
"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."
Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.
Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.
Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.
He has started 101 of his 103 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.
The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?
At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

Mauricio Pochettino has sent key members of his coaching staff to England in an early move to prepare for his role as Manchester United’s new head coach while he gets set to lead the US men’s national team for a final time.
Pochettino’s assistant Jesús Pérez, goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and athletic coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester soon after the US’s 6-0 victory over Haiti in Miami and in the run-up to United’s Premier League visit to Liverpool on Sunday, when Pochettino will take charge of a fourth English team for a first time. Before then, he will take charge of the US in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final with Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday.
Pochettino will have little time before his first game with United, with whom he has a signed a two-and-a-half year contract. He officially joins United on Wednesday.
“For me, it’s not difficult. I think we are well prepared to switch quick - ‌like a player, from the national team to the clubs,” Pochettino said on Monday. “From one game that you don’t play well to another that you need to be ready again. From one action to the next action.
“The business today is to be focusing here in ‌Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow. But for sure, in the moment that [we] finish that game, we are going to start ​to be 100% focused on our next project.”
Pochettino enjoys a close relationship with his staff, who have accompanied him through much of his time as a manager. Péréz, in particular, often appears alongside Pochettino at press conferences and other public events.

Dünya El Nino hava olayına karşı alarmda. Rekor sıcaklara ve rekor yağışlara neden olan El Nino için yeni uyarı Meteoroloji Mühendisi Mikdat Kadıoğlu'ndan geldi. Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu, 'Türkiye'de 2027 kışı nasıl geçecek? Çok kar yağacak mı?' sorularını yanıtladı.
Meteoroloji Mühendisi Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu, El Nino hava olaylarına dair yeni açıklamalarda bulundu. TGRT Haber'den Zeynep Gizem Er'e konuşan Kadıoğlu, '2027 kışı nasıl geçecek?' sorusunu da yanıtladı.
'Kasım ve aralık aylarının ortalamadan sıcak geçeceğine ilişkin bir tahmin, bütün kışın sıcak geçeceğini veya kar yağmayacağını göstermez. Mevsimlik tahminler, belirli bir dönemin genel eğilimini anlatır; tek tek günlerde yaşanacak hava olaylarını değil. WMO da bu ayrımı açıkça vurguluyor: Bunlar mevsimlik görünümlerdir, tekil olayların tahmini değildir.
Bunu şöyle düşünebiliriz: Bir ayın çoğu günü ılık geçerken birkaç gün çok soğuk olabilir. Dolayısıyla 'ortalamanın üzerinde sıcaklık' ile 'hiç soğuk olmayacak' aynı şey değildir. WMO’nun ekim –aralık görünümünde de ortalamadan sıcak bir dönem beklentisinin her yerin her gün ortalamadan sıcak olacağı anlamına gelmediği belirtiliyor.'
Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu'na göre 'Çok kar yağacak, şu illere kar yağacak gibi' cümleler için pek çok etken göz önünde bulundurulmalı. Kadıoğlu, sözlerine şöyle devam etti:
'El Niño’nun güçlü olması da tek başına Türkiye için bir kar haritası oluşturmaz. Etkiler mevsime, coğrafi konuma ve Hint ile Atlas okyanuslarındaki koşullar gibi diğer etkenlere göre değişebilir. Bu yüzden yalnızca El Niño’ya bakarak İstanbul ’a kar yağmayacak, şu illerde ağır kış olacak ya da bu bölgede kesin kuraklık yaşanacak demek, mevcut bilginin taşıyabileceğinden daha kesin konuşmaktır.
Hangi il ve bölgelerin daha fazla risk altında olduğunu söylemek için önce hangi riskten söz edildiği açıklanmalıdır: Yoğun kar mı, don mu, yağış azlığı mı, taşkın mı? Bunların her biri ayrı değerlendirme gerektirir. İl adı vererek yapılacak uyarıların dayanağı, ulusal ve yerel tahminler olmalıdır; küresel bir iklim olayının adı değil. Resmî uyarıların yetkili kaynağı ulusal meteoroloji servisleridir.'

Hollywood 'un usta oyuncusu Glenn Close, kariyeri boyunca sekiz kez aday gösterildiği halde bir türlü kazanamadığı Oscar heykelciğine sonunda kavuştu. 79 yaşındaki oyuncu, Sinema Sanatları ve Bilimleri Akademisi'nin Hollywood'daki Dolby Tiyatrosu'nda düzenlediği 17. Governors Ödülleri gecesinde Onursal Oscar'ını alırken gözyaşlarını tutamadı.
Close'u sahneye, "Tehlikeli İlişkiler" filminde birlikte rol aldığı John Malkovich davet etti. Hürriyet'in aktardığına göre Malkovich, uzun yıllardır dostu olan oyuncu için "O gerçek bir usta" dedi ve "Glenn, sınırları zorlamaktan asla korkmuyor; onun bu yönünü seviyorum" sözleriyle meslektaşını övdü. Salondaki davetliler Close'u uzun süre ayakta alkışladı.
Close, teşekkür konuşmasında eli boş döndüğü törenleri hatırlattı: "Dışarıdan biri olarak, kazanıp kazanmayacağım konusunda hiç endişelenmedim; gerçi bazı yıllar bir şansım olabileceğini düşünmüştüm." Oyuncu sözlerini "Asıl büyük onurun, o odada bulunmak olduğunu hep hissettim" diye sürdürdü.
Habertürk'ün aktardığına göre Close, Hollywood'da yapay zekâ kullanımının artmasına da değindi ve "Biz makine değiliz, kusurluyuz. Kurtuluşumuz da bu kusurlarımızdır" dedi. Oyuncu ödülünü, kendisi gibi oyuncu olan kızı Annie Starke'a ithaf etti.
Close'un Oscar serüveni, 1982 yapımı "Garp'a Göre Dünya" ile gelen En İyi Yardımcı Kadın Oyuncu adaylığıyla başladı. Oyuncu aynı dalda "The Big Chill" ve "The Natural" ile de aday gösterildi. "Öldüren Cazibe" (Fatal Attraction), "Tehlikeli İlişkiler" ve "Albert Nobbs" ise ona En İyi Kadın Oyuncu adaylığı getiren filmler arasında yer aldı. Sekiz adaylığın hiçbirinde ödül ona gitmedi.
Aynı gecede yönetmen Ridley Scott ile Disney'in ilk siyahi animatörü Floyd Norman da onurlandırıldı. Charlize Theron, Zendaya ve Olivia Wilde gibi isimlerin katıldığı Governors Ödülleri, ödül sezonunun açılışı sayılıyor.

Türkiye, UEFA Uluslar A Ligi'nde Fransa ile oynadığı son grup mücadelesini 2-1 kaybetti. Türk Milli Takımı grubunu son sırada ve puansız tamamladı.
Türkiye A Milli Futbol Takımı, tarihinde ilk kez mücadele ettiği UEFA Uluslar A Ligi 'nin altıncı ve son maçında deplasmanda Fransa'ya 2-1 mağlup oldu. Türkiye böylece A1 Grubu'nu hiç puan alamadan tamamlamış oldu.
Bordeaux kentindeki Matmut Atlantique Stadyumu'nda oynanan maçta Ay-Yıldızlıların tek golünü 90. dakikada Abdülkerim Bardakcı kaydetti. Türkiye, grubunu son sırada tamamladı.
Fransa, 49. dakikada kullanılan köşe vuruşunun ardından ceza sahasında yaşanan karambolde Emirhan Topçu'nun uzaklaştırmaya çalıştığı topun ağlara gitmesiyle öne geçti. Ev sahibi ekip, 80. dakikada Kroupi'nin golüyle farkı ikiye çıkardı.
A Millî Takım'ın tek golü ise 90. dakikada Abdülkerim Bardakcı'dan geldi.
Grubun diğer maçında Belçika, sahasında İtalya'yı 4-1 mağlup etti.
Bu sonuçlarla Fransa 13 puanla grup lideri olurken Belçika 12 puanla ikinci, İtalya ise 10 puanla üçüncü sırada yer aldı. A Millî Takım, UEFA Uluslar A Ligi'ndeki ilk sezonunu grubun son sırasında tamamladı.
Maçın ardından düzenlenen basın toplantısında A Milli Futbol Takımı Teknik Direktörü Sergen Yalçın açıklamalarda bulundu.
Dengeli bir maç olduğunu söyleyen Sergen Yalçın, "Oyuncular, ülkeleri için mücadele ediyorlar. Milli takımda oynuyorlar, ülke forması için mücadele ediyorlar. Bana göre bu mücadelenin sonunda da çok ciddi bir övgüyü hak ediyorlar. Maalesef biz kendi oyuncularımızı eleştirmeye, yerin dibine sokmaya çok alışık olduğumuz için gereken saygıyı ve alması gereken övgüyü çok vermiyoruz maalesef. Oyun planımız son derece doğruydu. 6 günde iki maç oynadık. İki farklı formatla oynadık iki maçı. Fransa maçında biraz rakibe göre pozisyon aldık. Fransa'nın ön tarafı çok güçlü belki de dünyanın en iyi oyuncu grubu var ön tarafta. Arka tarafı da bir o kadar sıkıntılı. Oyun planımız doğru işledi. Beraberliği yakalayabilirdik, öne geçebilirdik. Çok dengeli bir maç oldu. Her iki tarafın da kazanabileceği bir karşılaşmaydı. Ben ve ekibim bu iki maçta görmemiz gerekeni gördük. Bu süreç çok iyi oldu bizim için. Avrupa Şampiyonası kuralarından sonra milli takımımız hak ettiği yere gelecektir" ifadelerini kullandı.
